newsitem.title: USA: American, pilots to resume contract talks this week.
newsitem.headline: American, pilots to resume contract talks this week.

text.p: American Airlines and its pilots' union will resume contract talks this week at an undisclosed site, the two sides said Wednesday.
Officials of the Allied Pilots Association said the talks would start on Friday.
The talks will be mediated by Robert Harris, head of the Presidential Emergency Board that is trying to resolve the dispute between the nation's second-largest carrier and the 9,300 union pilots.

It will be the first meeting of American and its pilots since Feb. 14, when a week of intensive negotiations collapsed and the pilots went on strike, only to return to work minutes later after President Clinton established the three-member emergency board to try to resolve the dispute.

Pilots spokesman Gregg Overman said one day of talks was planned but it was likely the talks would be extended. The site of the negotiations was not disclosed. The last round drew heavy media coverage.
The emergency board met earlier this month and heard testimony from the airline and its pilots.

Harris and the board's two other members are to submit a proposed settlement to Clinton, American and the pilots on March 17. American and the pilots have 30 days to accept or reject the offer or reach a compromise.
If the pilots reject it, they are free to resume their strike. The company has said it would not operate without its pilots.

Congress could elect to step into the dispute, though that remains far from certain. It could pass a law ordering the pilots back to work, or calling on the two sides to accept the board's proposed settlement or enter into binding arbitration.
Pilots union President James Sovich said the union's board of directors would meet in Washington on March 21 to discuss the latest negotiations and the emergency board's proposals.
Two major issues separate American and its pilots.
One is pay. The union asked for an 11 percent increase to cover the past three years when it had no increase and the next four years. American has offered 6.5 percent.

The other is whether the union's pilots, who are paid an average of $120,000 a year, will fly the small regional jets American plans to buy for its commuter airline American Eagle. American wants to use lower-paid pilots that fly for American Eagle.
